name: Chair Pose
intro:
Chair Pose (Utkatasana) is a powerful standing yoga posture that builds strength, stability, and endurance. In this pose, the body mimics sitting on an imaginary chair, engaging the legs, core, and upper body simultaneously. It is widely practiced for strengthening muscles and improving balance while also boosting energy levels.

This pose activates major muscle groups including the thighs, calves, glutes, and shoulders. It also helps in improving posture by strengthening the spine and core. The upward stretch of the arms combined with the bent knees creates a dynamic tension in the body that enhances both strength and flexibility.

Regular practice of Chair Pose improves stamina, concentration, and body awareness. It also stimulates the heart and diaphragm, making it beneficial for circulation and breathing. Despite its simplicity, holding this pose can be challenging, making it highly effective for building both physical and mental resilience.

steps.text: Start by standing straight in Mountain Pose (Tadasana).
Raise your arms overhead with palms facing each other.
Bend your knees and lower your hips as if sitting on a chair.
Keep your chest lifted and spine straight.
Hold the position while keeping your weight on your heels.

benefits: Engages core muscles and strengthens the back
avoid: You have knee injuries or severe knee pain
You suffer from lower back problems
You have ankle instability or injuries
You experience dizziness or balance issues
You are recovering from recent surgery
You feel discomfort while holding the pose
